Subject: Budget gauge — monthly burn corridor & procurement checkpoints

Ava — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side based on the call: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary workload: clinical summarization + eligibility routing for patient support.
- Expected test window: 60–90 days.
- Usage estimate you gave: baseline ~0.8M tokens/month, with burst to ~3M in month-on-month growth if pilot expands.

Budget / pricing notes we took down
- Target unit economics you mentioned on the call: target ceiling of $2,500 per 1M tokens for the pilot phase.
- Procurement trigger: internal PO under $25k can be processed by your procurement team; anything above that requires req + legal review (~2–3 weeks).

What we propose
1) Send an updated pilot quote aligned to the 1M–3M token band with two lanes: a pilot lane priced at $2,500/1M tokens (month-to-month) and a committed band option with stepped pricing if you land on a multi-month commit.
2) If PO <= $25k: fast-track procurement (we can attach stub invoice).
3) If PO > $25k: we'll prep an SOW and parallel legal / procurement checklist to minimize lead time.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-pricing-2026.pdf (pricing + sample SOW outline)

Next steps for today
- Can you confirm that procurement will accept a PO up to $25k without additional redlines? (cc: procurement@stellarishealth.com)
- If yes, we’ll send a short-form invoice and provisioning checklist so your engineers can start smoke tests within 48 hours of PO receipt.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min sync if it helps move procurement along.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Thanks, Kimberly — great recap. A few clarifications from procurement and finance: 

1) Volume assumptions: finance is comfortable approving a pilot that targets 1.0–1.5M tokens/month for the initial 60-day window. If we see quality and latency hold, we could step to 2.5–3.0M in month 3.

2) Unit economics: finance has earmarked $2,500 per 1M tokens as the upper bound for the pilot. Anything below that is preferable.

3) PO thresholds: procurement confirms they can approve POs up to $25,000 internally (no legal redline) provided the terms are our standard vendor terms. Anything above $25k will require legal + procurement review and a short SOW. Lead time for >$25k is estimated 10–15 business days.

Action items from our side:
- Procurement requests a written quote (line-item) that shows: pilot lane pricing, estimated monthly tokens for the pilot, and a simple acceptance criteria for completing the 60-day test.
- If you can include a fast-start provisioning checklist and an optional SOW template (we saw the PDF you attached), that will help accelerate the >$25k path if we choose it.

Please cc Marcus D. (technical) for any engineering-rollout notes.

Best,
Ava Reynolds

Stellaris Health

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Ava — noted and here's how we'll proceed.

What I'll send you by EOD:
- A one-page line-item quote showing: pilot lane at $2,500/1M tokens, an estimated 1.0–1.5M tokens/month consumption band, and an estimated pilot spend range (month 1: ~$2.5k–$3.75k; month 2: similar; total pilot not to exceed PO amount you authorize).
- Fast-start provisioning checklist (steps to get API keys, shared prompset for smoke tests, test dataset guidance).
- Short SOW template for >$25k purchases (deliverables, acceptance criteria, timeline).

A couple of small clarifications that will help us shape the SOW and provisioning: 
- Acceptance criteria: is a latency SLA or sample-quality pass/fail acceptable, or would you prefer an engineering sign-off checklist?
- Billing: do you want Redwood to invoice monthly or to invoice the full pilot amount up front against the PO?

Procurement path we recommend (to minimize legal back-and-forth):
- Option A: PO <= $25k — procurement issues PO; we invoice and enable immediately (fast).
- Option B: PO > $25k — procurement issues a PO for the pilot and we attach the short SOW; we request parallel legal review and aim to reduce overall lead time to 7–10 business days by pre-populating standard clauses.

I’ve attached a purchase-lane-cheatsheet.xlsx that maps typical spend buckets to recommended Redwood buy lanes (pilot, reserved/dedicated, committed discounts).

If procurement confirms PO <= $25k is acceptable for the 60–90 day pilot, we can turn up keys within 48 hours of PO receipt.

Thanks — looping Aditya for provisioning and Jordan for committed-band pricing work.

Kim
